# dshctl

Control a **running** DeepSeek Harness (DSH) instance from scripts: create sessions in the
right wor

kspace, send prompts, wait for replies, and read back the conversation and the
memory blocks that we
re injected into it.
No clicking. No restart. No separate agent runtime.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Why this exists

DSH already ships a `headless` profile: one task, one answer, process exits. That is great
for batch

jobs, but it does not let you reach the instance you are actually using — the
desktop app with your
workspace, skills, plugins, and memory already loaded.

`dshctl` talks to that live instance's own `/api` Remote gateway, so anything you script
shows up in
the same GUI, in the same workspace, with the same plugins.
## Install

Python 3.10+, standard library only (one optional dependency for reading compressed
session logs):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Put the folder on `PATH` (Windows: `dshctl.cmd` is included) or call `python dshctl.py`.
## Commands
| Command | What it does |

| `dshctl instances` | Find running DSH processes and their API ports |
| `dshctl workspaces` | List

registered workspaces, marking the current directory |
| `dshctl sessions [--limit N] [--all]` | Li

st sessions with state, cwd, title |
| `dshctl new [--cwd DIR] [--workspace ID] [--preset NAME]` | C

reate a session |
| `dshctl ask "TEXT" [--timeout S]` | Create a session in the current workspace, s

end a prompt, print the reply |
| `dshctl send SESSION "TEXT" [--wait] [--mode queue\|steer]` | Send

to an existing session |
| `dshctl history SESSION [--chars N] [--full]` | Read the user/assistant

conversation |
| `dshctl memory SESSION [--json]` | Show the memory blocks injected into that sessio

versation |
| `dshctl memory SESSION [--json]` | Show the memory blocks injected into that session |
`--port`, `--json`, and `--token` work before or after the subcommand.
## How it works

**Port discovery.** DSH binds a fresh HTTP port on every launch (we observed 63195 → 49890).
`dshctl

` never hardcodes it: it lists listening ports owned by the `DeepSeek Harness`
process, then confirm

s the API port by the fact that an unauthenticated request returns
`401`.
**Authentication.** Two paths:

1. **Official launch token** — pass `--token` (or set `DSH_API_TOKEN`) with the token from the
URL D

SH prints/opens at startup. `dshctl` does `GET /?token=…`, receives the signed
session cookie from `

Set-Cookie`, and uses it. No local secret is read.
2. **Local fallback** — if no token is given, `ds

hctl` reads the `client-connection/browser-session`
signing secret from `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` a

nd mints an equivalent cookie with the
same `v1.HMAC-SHA256` scheme DSH itself uses. The secret is r

ead locally and never
transmitted anywhere.
**Wire format.** Requests are `POST /api/<method>` with a client-request envelope:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

**Workspace attachment — the trap.** `session/create` accepts either `cwd` or `workspaceId`.
Passing

only `cwd` gives the session the right directory but does **not** attach it to the
workspace, so it

never shows up in the sidebar. DSH only calls `attachSession` when the
request carries a `workspace

Id`. `dshctl` resolves the current directory to a registered
workspace first, and only falls back to
`cwd` (with a warning) for unregistered directories.

**Reading logs.** Session records live at
`~/.dsh/sessions/<workspace>/<sessionId>/session.v4.jsonl.

zstd` — zstd-compressed JSONL.
Assistant text lives under `data.message.content`; user text under `d

ata.content`. Anything
that is not a plain `text` part (reasoning, tool calls) is skipped.
## Use case: verifying what memory a keyword recalls
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`ask` with `--no-wait` returns immediately; `memory` then shows exactly which notes were
injected fo

r that prompt. Useful when you are tuning retrieval thresholds, or when you want
proof that a plugin

actually injected something (the log line says "injected", the session
record shows *what*).
## Prior art / similar tools
DSH is open source (MIT) with a large ecosystem. Related projects worth knowing:
- deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness — the harness itself; official `headless` profile, `sdk-minimal` prof

ile and SDK packages
- ccch1mneyyy/dsh-Go — run DSH on a phone and remote-control your computer
- to

mmy0103/obelisk — make past sessions/subagents queryable
- YouHui1/dsh-sessions-diagnosis — diagnose

sessions that stopped opening
- yamingmou/dsh-log-contract — session log contract checks
- Larrtrof
fen/harnessbridge — session migration/bridge

`dshctl` is deliberately narrow: a small CLI that drives the *already running* instance and
reads ba

ck what it recorded. If you need a runtime of your own, use the official `headless`
or `sdk-minimal`

d. If you need a runtime of your own, use the official `headless`
or `sdk-minimal` profiles instead.
## Limits

- Requires a running DSH desktop/web instance. Headless runs have no HTTP gateway to attach to.
- Po

rt discovery uses `tasklist`/`netstat`, so it is Windows-first. Elsewhere, pass `--port`.
- `history

` / `memory` need `zstandard`.
- Internal APIs. Method names and the log format are version-specific

(`session.v4`), and an
upgrade may change them. Treat this as a userland tool, not a stable SDK.
-

Reads your own local machine and your own credentials. Do not point it at machines you do
not own.
